deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page: no formulas, computations or derivations. The folio is a set of excerpts that Riemann copied from Johann Friedrich Herbart's philosophical works. The references point to Hartenstein's edition of Herbart's Sämmtliche Werke, abbreviated 'W.' with volume and page. The excerpts are:
(1) Psychologie als Wissenschaft, Bd. 2, Vorrede/VIII (W. VI, 6). Plato already grasped the 'principle of finitude' so as to impose no limits beyond those the visible universe sets. He placed things outside God as regards their being, against Spinoza, yet subjected them to Providence as regards what they are and mean for us.
(2) Psych. Bd. 1, §78 (W. V, 262). Without Herbart's practical philosophy his psychology is misunderstood. He rejects innate rights, innate moral feeling and the categorical imperative, since all innate forms are psychologically impossible. Moral feeling is instead derived as the combined effect of the practical ideas, which rest on aesthetic judgments. Hence he does not fear the 'psychological mechanism'.
(3) Psych. Bd. 1, IX (W. V, 195). Herbart started from the investigation of the Ich. This produced the 'Methode der Beziehungen', a general method for metaphysical problems. It also gave a concept of 'the real' (das Reale) definite enough to be subject to calculation. Only later did he note that the principle could be presented as a hypothesis for readers not to be burdened with metaphysics.
(4) Allgemeine Metaphysik I, §25, general remark to chapter 2 (W. III, 96). Leibniz's monadology will return in altered form. The spiritualism of psychologists and the atomism of modern chemists both contain truth. Idealism was a necessary transition.
(5) Met. I §27 (W. III, 105-106) and W. III, 115, plus §28. The first chief error of old metaphysics is tearing apart the relations of concepts for the sake of logical order. One should be guided by relations, not logical similarities. The second chief error is defective connection to the given.
(6) Psych. Bd. 2, §138 (W. VI, 259). Ichheit cannot stand in strict speculative rigor. The method of relations exposes the root of the contradiction, modifies the concept minimally, and sketches the concept it must turn into.
The page belongs to Riemann's known study of Herbart, alongside the previous page (Herbart's Hemmung/Verschmelzung psychology) and the next page (Herbart on Leibniz, Plato's Timaeus, chemistry). The only quasi-mathematical content is Herbart's remark that the concept of the real can be 'subjected to calculation'. This alludes to Herbart's mathematical psychology, which is not worked out here.

results.what: Excerpts from Herbart's Psychologie als Wissenschaft and Allgemeine Metaphysik on the method of relations, the concept of the real, rejection of innate forms, and monadology/atomism
results.modern_name: Herbartian metaphysics and psychology (method of relations, 'Reale')

deep.surprise_reason: These are reading notes copying Herbart's text, with no original mathematics. Riemann's study of and allegiance to Herbart ("Ich bin Herbartianer in Psychologie und Erkenntnistheorie") is well documented in the published Nachlass fragments on Naturphilosophie.
transcription_corrections: Second excerpt likely begins 'Wer meine praktische Philosophie verschmäht, dessen Gemüth ...' (Herbart's wording), not 'Meine praktische Philosophie verschmäht: dessen ...'.
In the Platon excerpt, 'was sie für uns sind, bedeuten, und wirken' appears more likely than 'und was sie sind'. The image shows a short verb, not a repeated 'was sie sind'.
'Metaphysik I, Anmerkung zum zweiten Kapitel W. III' is struck through in the manuscript, leaving only ', 115'. This is correctly marked, but the struck text also includes 'zum zweiten Kapitel'.
'der Begriff des Realen vorzustellen [?]' is uncertain; the underlined phrase may be 'des Realen herzustellen' or similar. It should be checked against Herbart, Psych. als Wiss. I (W. V, 195).
'unzweckmässigen [?] logischen Ordnung' is plausible and should be checked against Herbart, Allg. Metaphysik §27.
